examples.en: I had jeyukbokkeum near the office for lunch.

examples.ko: 제육볶음은 밥이랑 같이 먹으면 정말 맛있어요.
examples.en: Jeyukbokkeum is really delicious with rice.

examples.ko: 상추에 제육볶음을 싸 먹으면 더 맛있어요.
examples.en: It tastes even better when you wrap jeyukbokkeum in lettuce.

examples.ko: 저는 매운 제육볶음이 좋아서 자주 시켜요.
examples.en: I like spicy jeyukbokkeum, so I order it often.
Please pack one jeyukbokkeum lunch box to go.

examples.ko: 어머니가 만든 제육볶음 맛이 아직도 생각나요.
examples.en: I still remember the taste of the jeyukbokkeum my mother made.

explain: 돼지고기를 고추장 양념에 볶은 매콤한 반찬이에요. 식당 메뉴에서는 줄여서 '제육'이라고도 하고, 백반집이나 도시락 메뉴에서 자주 볼 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I'll have one jeyuk, please.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식당 메뉴에서 '제육볶음'을 줄여 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short form of jeyukbokkeum used on restaurant menus.

phrases.en: I will eat jeyuk rice bowl for lunch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밥 위에 제육볶음을 올린 한 그릇 음식이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A one-bowl dish with jeyukbokkeum served on top of rice.

phrases.en: I made jeyukbokkeum at home on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리할 때는 '만들다'나 '하다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 'make' or 'do' when cooking it.

explain_en: It is a spicy dish of pork stir-fried in a red pepper paste marinade. On restaurant menus it is often shortened to '제육', and you often see it at set-meal restaurants and on lunch box menus.

en: to pan-fry; to simmer down in a little sauce

examples.en: Mom pan-fries kimchi in a frying pan.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날에는 부침개를 지져 먹어요.
examples.en: On rainy days we fry pancakes and eat them.
I pan-fried the bindaetteok in oil.
I pan-fry the tofu until golden and add the sauce.

examples.ko: 양념을 넣고 자작하게 지진 두부가 맛있어요.
examples.en: Tofu braised with seasoning and just a little broth is tasty.
What will you cook in the pan tonight?

explain: 기름을 조금 두르고 부치거나, 국물을 적게 해서 졸이듯 익히는 요리에 써요. 국물이 많은 요리는 '끓이다'라고 해서 구분해요.

phrases.en: I pan-fried tofu and ate it for dinner.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 먹다'를 붙여 지져서 바로 먹는다는 뜻이에요. 집에서 간단히 해 먹을 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-아/어 먹다' means pan-frying something and eating it, often used for simple home cooking.

phrases.en: I pan-fried the fish in oil.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기름을 두르고 익히는 방법을 분명히 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Makes clear that the food is cooked in a little oil.

phrases.en: I like the smell of Mom pan-frying pancakes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여서 지지는 모습이나 소리, 냄새를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-는' it describes the sight, sound, or smell of pan-frying.

explain_en: It is used for frying in a little oil or simmering a dish down until little broth remains. Dishes with a lot of broth use '끓이다' instead.

t90.ax: I pan-fried the bindaetteok in oil.

examples.en: One caramel-flavored ice cream, please.
The caramel sticks to my teeth, so it's hard to eat.
Please add caramel syrup to my coffee.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 캐러멜을 먹다가 이가 빠졌어요.
examples.en: When I was little, my tooth came out while I was eating caramel.
This pudding tastes sweet like caramel.
Caramel is too sweet, so I only eat a little.

explain: '카라멜'이라고 쓰는 사람도 있지만 표준 표기는 '캐러멜'이에요. 씹어 먹는 사탕뿐 아니라 설탕을 녹여 만든 소스나 시럽 맛을 말할 때도 써요.

phrases.en: I put caramel sauce in my coffee.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사탕이 아니라 설탕을 녹여 만든 소스를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the sauce made from melted sugar, not the candy.

phrases.en: Please give me just one caramel.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 사탕은 '알'로 세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Small candies are counted with 'al'.

phrases.en: Caramel sticks to my teeth when I chew it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사탕을 먹는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the action of chewing the candy.

explain_en: Some people write '카라멜', but the standard spelling is '캐러멜'. It refers not only to the chewy candy but also to the flavor of sauces and syrups made from melted sugar.

examples.en: I took one bite and said it was delicious.
I ate the whole cake in one mouthful.
Please cut the vegetables into bite-sized pieces.
The child begged for just one bite.

examples.ko: 한입씩 나눠 먹으면 모두 맛볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: If we share it bite by bite, everyone can taste it.
I stuffed a mouthful of ramyeon in and smiled.

explain: '한입에 먹다'는 한 번에 다 먹는다는 쓰임이고, '한입 먹다'는 조금 베어 먹는다는 쓰임이에요. 조사에 따라 달라지니까 주의하세요. '한입만'은 조금만 달라고 할 때 자주 써요.

phrases.en: Please give me just one bite of that.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조금만 먹고 싶다고 부탁할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to ask for just a little taste.

phrases.en: I ate the dumpling in one bite.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 번에 다 먹는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means eating it all at once.

phrases.en: I cut the fruit into bite-sized pieces.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 번에 먹기 좋은 크기를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A size that's easy to eat at once.

explain_en: '한입에 먹다' means to eat all of it at once, while '한입 먹다' means to take a bite. The particle changes the meaning, so be careful. '한입만' is used when asking for just a little taste.

examples.en: I meet my friends at the basketball court on weekends.
A new basketball court opened next to the school.
It rained, so the basketball court floor is slippery.

examples.ko: 농구장은 밤 열 시에 문을 닫아요.
examples.en: The basketball court closes at ten at night.
There were many people at the basketball court, so I waited.
We played basketball at an outdoor court.

explain: 농구를 하는 장소를 말하고, 축구장, 야구장처럼 '-장'이 붙은 말과 같은 짝이에요. 농구 경기를 크게 하는 곳은 '농구 경기장'이라고도 해요. 길가에 있는 작은 곳은 보통 '농구장'이라고 말해요.

phrases.en: I watched a game at the basketball arena on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경기를 크게 하는 큰 곳을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a large venue where games are held.

phrases.en: After school I go to the basketball court with a friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동하러 가는 장소로 가장 흔하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to name the place you go to play.
phrases.en_equiv: to go to the basketball court

phrases.en: My house is next to the basketball court.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위치를 말할 때 '옆', '앞'과 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used with 옆 or 앞 to describe a location.

explain_en: It is a place for playing basketball, in the same group as 축구장 and 야구장. A large venue for games can also be called '농구 경기장'. A small court out in the neighborhood is usually just called '농구장'.

examples.ko: 오늘 저녁에 가수가 라이브 방송을 해요.
examples.en: The singer is doing a live broadcast this evening.

examples.ko: 콘서트에서 라이브로 노래를 들으니 정말 좋았어요.
examples.en: Hearing the song live at the concert was really great.

examples.ko: 이 카페에서는 주말마다 라이브 공연을 해요.
examples.en: This cafe holds live performances every weekend.

examples.ko: 친구가 라이브에서 제 이름을 불러 줬어요.
examples.en: My friend called out my name during the livestream.

examples.ko: 라이브가 끝난 뒤에 영상을 다시 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: After the live ends, you can watch the video again.

examples.ko: 이 곡은 앨범보다 라이브가 더 멋있어요.
examples.en: This song sounds cooler live than on the album.

explain: 방송이나 공연이 지금 바로 이뤄질 때 써요. '라이브 방송', '라이브 공연'이 가장 많아요. 녹화한 것은 '녹화', 나중에 다시 보는 것은 '다시보기'라고 해요.

phrases.en: My friend posted a live video yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 찍는 영상을 바로 보여 주는 영상이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A video that is shown while it is being filmed.

phrases.en: I listen to music at a live music cafe on weekends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가수가 직접 노래하는 카페를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A cafe where singers perform in person.

phrases.en: I watched the soccer match live.
phrases.nuance_ko: 녹화가 아니라 지금 일어나는 것을 볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when watching something as it happens, not a recording.

explain_en: It is used when a broadcast or performance is happening right now. 라이브 방송 and 라이브 공연 are the most common. Recorded material is 녹화, and watching it later is 다시보기.

en: to be played; to be shown

examples.en: That movie will be shown next week.

examples.ko: 이 영화관에서 한국 영화가 상영되고 있어요.
examples.en: A Korean film is showing at this theater.
The movie shown today was fun.
Ads played before the film was shown.

examples.ko: 단편 영화 세 편이 상영될 거예요.
examples.en: Three short films will be screened.
That work was screened overseas too.

explain: 영화가 주어일 때 '상영되다'를 써요. 영화관에서 영화를 틀어 주는 것이 '상영하다'예요. 연극이나 콘서트는 '상영' 대신 '공연'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 그 영화는 지금 극장에서 상영되고 있어요.
phrases.en: That movie is being shown in theaters now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 영화가 극장에서 나오는 중일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when a film is currently showing in theaters.

phrases.en: This movie is showing now.
phrases.nuance_ko: '상영되다'보다 짧고, 영화관 안내나 광고에서 많이 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shorter than 상영되다, and common in cinema notices and ads.

phrases.example: 그 영화는 우리 동네에서 상영되지 않아요.
phrases.en: That movie isn't shown in my neighborhood.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영화가 어느 곳에서 나오지 않을 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, for when a film isn't playing somewhere.

explain_en: Use 상영되다 when the movie is the subject. Showing a film in a theater is 상영하다. For plays or concerts, say 공연 instead of 상영.

examples.en: My child is totally hooked on hidden picture games.
I found five cats in the hidden picture puzzle.
There is a hidden picture puzzle on the back page of the book.
You need good eyes to be good at hidden picture games.

examples.ko: 동생과 누가 먼저 찾나 숨은그림찾기를 했어요.
examples.en: My sibling and I did a hidden picture puzzle to see who would find it first.
This hidden picture puzzle was so hard that I gave up.

explain: '숨은 그림'이 아니라 '숨은그림찾기'를 한 단어로 붙여 써요. '숨은그림찾기를 하다', '숨은그림찾기를 풀다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.example: 비 오는 날 집에서 숨은그림찾기를 했어요.
phrases.en: On a rainy day, we did a hidden picture puzzle at home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이 놀이를 한다고 말할 때 가장 기본으로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic way to say you do this puzzle.
phrases.en_equiv: to do a hidden picture puzzle

phrases.en: I bought my child a hidden picture book.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숨은그림찾기가 담긴 책을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A book full of hidden picture puzzles.

phrases.en: This hidden picture puzzle is too hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제의 어려움을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about how hard a puzzle is.
phrases.en_equiv: the hidden picture puzzle is hard

explain_en: It is written as one word, '숨은그림찾기', not '숨은 그림 찾기'. People say '숨은그림찾기를 하다' or '숨은그림찾기를 풀다'.

examples.en: An art festival is held in our neighborhood.
Students danced at the art festival.
The art festival goes on for three days.
I saw the art festival poster at the library.
Do you want to go to the autumn art festival with me?
I am busy these days preparing for the art festival.

explain: '-제'는 축제나 큰 행사 이름에 붙어요. 예술제, 영화제, 음악제처럼 써요. 행사는 '열리다', 가는 것은 '참가하다'나 '가다'와 같이 써요.

phrases.en: An art festival will be held at the school next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사가 시작되고 진행된다고 말할 때 '열리다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 열리다 to say that the event takes place.

phrases.en: I'm taking part in the art festival this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구경하는 것이 아니라 직접 무대나 행사에 함께할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when you take part yourself, not just watch.
phrases.en_equiv: to take part in the art festival

phrases.en: I went to the art festival with a friend on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구경하러 갈 때 쓰는 가장 쉬운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The simplest way to say you went to see the festival.
phrases.en_equiv: to go to the art festival

explain_en: The ending '-제' attaches to the names of festivals and large events, such as '예술제', '영화제' and '음악제'. An event '열리다', and you go with '참가하다' or '가다'.

examples.en: I saw a turtle at the zoo.
A turtle walks slowly.
Tortoises are animals that live a long time.
The child slept hugging a toy turtle.
The tortoise and the hare had a race.
I fed the turtle at the beach.

explain: '거북이'라는 말도 같이 써요. 아주 느린 걸음을 비유할 때는 '거북이걸음'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: Turtles live a really long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '거북'과 같은 동물이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '거북이'를 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the same animal. 거북이 is more common in everyday speech.

phrases.en: The traffic is so bad the cars are crawling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아주 느리게 가는 모습을 비유할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively for moving very slowly.

phrases.en: A sea turtle is swimming in the ocean.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바다에 사는 거북을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers specifically to turtles that live in the sea.

explain_en: The form 'geobugi' is also used. A very slow pace is described figuratively as 'geobugigeoreum' (turtle walk).

examples.en: The child blew up a balloon and it popped.
The balloon floated away into the sky.

examples.ko: 생일 파티에 고무풍선을 열 개 달았어요.
examples.en: I hung ten balloons at the birthday party.
A rubber balloon pops when it touches a needle.
I wrote a name on a balloon and gave it as a gift.
Please buy me just one balloon.

explain: 그냥 '풍선'이라고 해도 보통 같은 물건을 말해요. 불다, 터지다, 날아가다 같은 말과 같이 많이 써요.

phrases.en: I blew up balloons at the birthday party.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고무풍선을 줄여서 부르는 흔한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The common, shorter way to say 고무풍선.

phrases.en: The balloon suddenly popped and I was startled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 풍선이 펑 하고 터질 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation for a balloon bursting.

phrases.en: The children let their balloons fly into the sky.
phrases.nuance_ko: 풍선을 놓아서 하늘로 보낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when letting balloons go up into the sky.

explain_en: Just saying '풍선' usually refers to the same thing. It goes with verbs like 불다 (blow up), 터지다 (pop) and 날아가다 (fly away).

examples.en: On the weekend I went to the public bathhouse with my father.
At a public bathhouse, you shower and then get into the tub.
Public bathhouses have decreased a lot these days.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 공중목욕탕에서 먹던 바나나우유가 생각나요.
examples.en: I remember the banana milk I drank at the bathhouse as a kid.

examples.ko: 공중목욕탕 가는 날은 온 가족이 일찍 일어났어요.
examples.en: On bathhouse days, the whole family woke up early.

examples.ko: 이 동네에는 오래된 공중목욕탕이 하나 있어요.
examples.en: There is one old public bathhouse in this neighborhood.

explain: 일상에서는 그냥 '목욕탕'이라고 많이 말해요. 여러 사람이 함께 쓰는 곳이라 공중도덕을 지켜야 해요.

phrases.en: I often go to the local bathhouse.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 더 많이 쓰는 짧은 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The shorter word used more often in daily life.

phrases.en: The public bathhouse is crowded on weekends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 많을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation for when there are many people.

phrases.en: I soaked my body in warm water at the public bathhouse.
phrases.nuance_ko: 탕 안에 들어가 쉬는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes getting into the bath to relax.

explain_en: In daily speech people often just say '목욕탕'. Many people share the space, so you need to follow public etiquette.

t90.ax: Public bathhouses have decreased a lot these days.

examples.en: The baby kicks every time I change the diaper.
Someone kept kicking in their sleep, so I slept poorly.
I kicked hard at the ball, but missed.

examples.ko: 아기가 좋아서 다리를 흔들며 발길질하고 있어요.
examples.en: The baby is happily waving and kicking its legs.
Please don't kick around on the bed.

examples.ko: 발길질하면 다칠 수 있으니까 장난으로도 하지 마세요.
examples.en: Kicking can hurt someone, so don't do it even as a joke.

explain: '발로 차다'와 달리 발을 계속 휘두르거나 여러 번 차는 느낌이 있어요. '발길질을 하다'로도 말해요. 수영에서 발을 움직이는 동작은 보통 '발차기'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The child kicked while crying.
phrases.nuance_ko: '발길질하다'를 '을/를'을 넣어 말하는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The same verb with the object particle added.

phrases.en: I kicked the ball far away with my foot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 번 차는 동작에 더 잘 어울리는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits better for a single kick.

phrases.en: The baby kicks wildly in bed.
phrases.nuance_ko: '마구'를 붙이면 계속 세게 차는 느낌이 강해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '마구' stresses wild, nonstop kicking.

explain_en: Unlike '발로 차다', it gives a feeling of swinging the feet around or kicking repeatedly. You can also say '발길질을 하다'. In swimming, the leg motion is usually called '발차기'.

t90.ax: Please don't kick around on the bed.
